steps.content:
September 12, N.F. 115, 02:00 PM
City Council
At the chairman's podium, Augustus flips through the agenda, glancing at one page, discarding the next. The pages litter the ground around her feet like fallen leaves.
Armed soldiers of the Shattered Blade stand in formation behind her, their weapons raised and trained on the captive councilors.
The sight is eerily familiar.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Augustus! That's enough!
She lifts her head, her gaze slow and deliberate, finding the Speaker of the City Council. His face is a mask of fury, his own body a shield for the trembling officials he protects.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: ...Save the heroics, Speaker. They don't deserve it. They're neither your comrades nor noble councilors. They can't even be called law-abiding citizens.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: These are scavengers. Parasites. The shadows lurking beneath your beloved city are vast. Step aside and let me clean the gutter. You keep your hands clean.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: ...I won't allow it. The war is over. Your emergency powers are revoked. You don't get to bypass the law and execute your own brand of justice!

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: You should be DisCity's protector. Drop your blade and return to the order you should be upholding!

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: And I believe cutting out the tumor is the fastest way to restore that order and protect your city-state. My methods are just more effective.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Your "effective methods" are a slippery slope! Today it's them, tomorrow it's anyone you please! Your violence has no oversight, no guarantee of justice.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: This system—these rules—were built over the years for this exact reason! This simply can't be replaced by violence or individual action. No one's strength, no one's wisdom, is enough for that burden!

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Stop this, General Augustus! We fought side-by-side in the war. I know the soldier you are—honorable, noble! Don't prove the rumors right! Don't stray down this wrong path!
Without a word, Augustus strikes open the iron box at her feet. The lid flies open, and she upends it, scattering a pile of "evidence" before Max King.
It's a collection of intelligence, a dossier of slander. But it is the final photograph—Adrian, pale and still in a hospital bed—that makes his eyes widen in raw shock.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: ...Are you threatening me?!

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Not me. This is a gift from your many, many "well-wishers." Hoping to help me bring you down.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Every single piece of this "evidence" could work perfectly within your precious legal order to democratically destroy you. Ironic, isn't it?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: The "order" you defend doesn't want a righteous man, Speaker. It prefers someone ruthless and insolent like me.
She borrows a light from one of her subordinates and drops it to the ground. Right before Max King's eyes, she watches the slander curl and blacken into ash.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: My patience has limits. I've waited. I played the long game. Gathered evidence, filed reports, and delivered it all on a silver platter to the courts.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: And poof. It vanished. Buried carefully. The witnesses I "exposed"? I had to send my own people to protect them from being silenced... by your "order."

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: You want to know the real tragedy, Speaker?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Even after I held my nose and wallowed in their muck... even with the ruthless methods I'm employing now... I still couldn't see the whole picture. I barely scratched the surface.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: What a vast web... How deep it goes... You've seen the real battlefield of guns and fire. Now open your eyes to the one in the shadows. Where they kill without spilling a single drop of blood.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: While you cling to your principles, what have our enemies become? Do you really think your sacred, inviolable "faith" is a weapon that can win this war?
His eyes track the photograph as it curls and blackens in the fire, his stare unbreaking. A long silence hangs in the air. Then, his jaw tightens, and he lifts his head.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: I know the corruption is terrifying. I swim in it every day. I know it better than anyone... And so do you, General.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: You want to solve this the old DisCorps way, with brutal, efficient violence to enforce your own will. But you're smart enough to see it. The shadows hold more than one kind of monster...

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Look in the mirror. Marshal Dravyn's shadow is already falling over you. Doesn't that scare you, General?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: ...You really are as ${PlayerName} said. Upright. Brave. A true comrade. Honestly, I worry a bullet with your name on it is waiting in the wings.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: The DisCorps might have to keep you on a leash for your own good.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Take him away.

steps.speaker: Soldier
steps.content: Roger that!

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: You...! Let go of me!!

With the Speaker dragged away, the remaining councilors are a portrait of pure fear, trembling, cowering, faces drained of color. Augustus's focus shifts to an abandoned camera left aside. It shudders, then lifts from the ground, floating on a wave of magnetic energy to stop directly in front of her.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: ...Well then. It took me years to reclaim my blades. The war with the Outland can wait. A different battle needs fighting first... and I have all the time in the world.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Hyenas... maggots... beasts of the Sillage Society. You've trampled lives, stolen the city's noble cause, and manipulated the loyalty of better men and women. You've embedded yourselves like parasites, sucking this city dry for far too long.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: But now... the troop of ghosts has returned from hell. The time for reckoning is here. And I will see to it... until the end!
Her declaration sets the city ablaze. As the reality of the imminent storm dawns on its citizens, a select few begin to prepare.
[Scene Change]

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: This is what power does to people. She just realized she could use violence, that she could dispense her own justice, and that she could bypass any opposition... so she did. That's the inevitable logic of power.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: She found the formula to convert violence into authority. And in that, she found what feels like total freedom. Heh. It's Dravyn's playbook all over again... History doesn't just repeat itself; it follows a script.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: Chief, you need to step back. Your integrity used to be an asset in her eyes, but now it might just be a thorn in her path.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: Use the goodwill she still has for you. Stay close, and stay quiet. Telling her what you really think now is just volunteering to be her next example. Wait. As long as she's willing to listen to you, there's a chance.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: If you challenge her directly, I fear you'll be crushed by her, just like the others.
[Scene Change]
Most people feel utterly bewildered.

steps.speaker: Civilian
steps.content: Dravyn's... heir? The stories are true? She's taking power? What were those days even like? Surely Paradeisos won't just stand by and let this happen?

steps.speaker: Civilian
steps.content: They probably will. Paradeisos only intervenes when Mania flares up. As long as the streets are quiet, they don't care who's in charge. Rumor is they've already shaken hands with the General. The Speaker is an outdated concept, after all.

steps.speaker: Civilian
steps.content: ...So what do we do? How long will this last? What happens to us now...?
Only a rare few have not forgotten their anger.
[Badly injured but still raging at the camera]

steps.speaker: Barry Orwell
steps.content: Justice?! Don't you dare call this justice!! This is the raw exercise of power, masquerading as law! If she can shred the legal code to punish her enemies today, she will turn it on any one of you tomorrow! This is not justice; it is the birth of a tyranny!

steps.speaker: Barry Orwell
steps.content: You can hear me, right, Catherine Augustus Andohar?! I will not be your prop! I will not be the "victim" you use to justify breaking our world to your will! I reject your so-called justice! Do you hear me?!

steps.speaker: Barry Orwell
steps.content: You... you hypocrite! You stood where I stand and told me to have faith! You spoke of a better system, of change! So tell me, how are you any different from Dravyn?!
[Cut to EDGE]

EDGE-03: Are we certain intervention is unnecessary? Multiple departments are concerned this could trigger unforeseen social instability.

EDGE-05: Necessary? This appears to be another routine power transfer in the lower levels. There's no risk of triggering a Mania crisis. The structural weaknesses from Dravyn's era won't resurface.
EDGE-05: Moreover, from a purely practical perspective...
EDGE-05: DisCity currently relies on her forces for security, doesn't it?

EDGE-02: Hmm... We have two members here familiar with her. Any observations?
EDGE-02: 01. You must have anticipated this situation.

EDGE-01: Well... Rational analysis tends to prove unreliable when applied to her. The margin for error is substantial.
EDGE-01: That said, I concur with 05's assessment. The probability of a significant crisis remains low.

EDGE-01: Based on intuitive observation, both the duration and impact of this disturbance should remain contained. Wouldn't you agree?
EDGE-01: ...Given your understanding of her.

EDGE-06: ...
EDGE-06: My assessment is irrelevant. Run your own calculations.
[Switch Scene]
But you can't keep up with her.

The Shattered Blade sweeps through the city like a storm of steel; there are simply too many to arrest, too many to process through interrogation. The only way to dominate this new battlefield is with sheer, overwhelming speed.
At her former residence, before the tightly shut doors, only Iron Mask stands guard, as if he has been waiting for you, and you alone.

steps.speaker: Iron Mask
steps.content: She's not here.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: When will she come back? I've been here quite a few times. Knowing her, she wouldn't stay away from you all for long.

steps.speaker: Iron Mask
steps.content: The General is occupied.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The situation is getting very dangerous. She needs to know. If you don't think I'm the right one to tell her, then you should.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You... You're the Rancors. You're Augustus's most trusted allies. It's your duty to steer her right.

steps.speaker: Iron Mask
steps.content: ...You're mistaken. Rancors are not her "most trusted allies." We are her swords, shattered blades, collected from across the world.

steps.speaker: Iron Mask
steps.content: To control a frenzied weapon, a commander cannot show weakness. More than trust or dependence, we need her strength. Unrivaled.

options: And you're not afraid she'll end up isolated?!

choices.text: And you're not afraid she'll end up isolated?!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Whether they're with the Sillage Society or not, they targeted Barry to deceive her. To isolate her, so they can manipulate her later.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Would you really let your commander charge into the battlefield alone, too stubborn to listen?
Iron Mask remains silent, but his gaze lingers on you.

steps.speaker: Iron Mask
steps.content: We obey our commander, support her, and trust her. Absolutely. As for what you mentioned...

steps.speaker: Iron Mask
steps.content: If you care that much, then you should be the one to do it.
[Switch Scene]
Once more, you return empty-handed. But waiting for you back at the MBCC is a figure you never expected to see.
[Empty Scene for 1 second] Display portrait

steps.speaker: Commander-in-Chief
steps.content: ...The FAC doesn't involve itself in political struggles. What she's doing won't last much longer. This will be over soon.

steps.speaker: Commander-in-Chief
steps.content: But if you still insist on seeing her...

steps.speaker: Commander-in-Chief
steps.content: Then I'll give you these. Just some old things that should have been discarded long ago.
You accept the stack of aged letters. The pages are filled with a script you quickly recognize as an antiquated cipher, a language within a language.
Yet even through the unreadable code, the emotion is palpable—in the angry press of ink that has scarred the paper, and in the stark, familiar signatures that mark each page.

<size=40><i>
—Dravyn

—Adrian
You read through the letters, the silence in the room broken only by the rustle of old paper. When you finish, you lay the stack heavily on your lap before raising your eyes to meet the elder's gaze.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: No matter where she's gone, or what she believes now... I'll find a way to reach her. I promise.
[Switch Scene]

steps.speaker: Iron Mask
steps.content: He's been here many times. Are you really not going to see him?
steps.female_content: She's been here many times. Are you really not going to see her?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: No.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: We'll talk after this is over.

steps.speaker: Iron Mask
steps.content: I see.
Iron Mask lowers his head.

steps.speaker: Iron Mask
steps.content: But he doesn't see it that way.
steps.female_content: But she doesn't see it that way.

steps.content: A message from the MBCC is presented to her. Augustus accepts it, her eyes swiftly parsing the text within.
<i>I've found a quiet place for the <color=#fb9259>next round</color>. I'll be waiting.<i>
[Scene change] Several days later

September 17, N.F. 115, 09:00 PM
Eastside Suburbs, Nameless Bar
You step back into the bar. The amber glow, the soft melody—everything seems unchanged, yet holds in a new silence. The stool where Augustus sat last time is empty.
This time, the owner welcomes you with a gentle smile, offering a glass of Augustus's favorite cocktail.

steps.speaker: Owner
steps.content: A spark of life returns to their dull eyes. The dying embers of their old dreams reignite, kindling a new flame of hope that spreads among the townsfolk.

steps.speaker: Owner
steps.content: She's always been cautious about her affairs. She finds me directly. Never leaves a thread for me to pull. I'm sorry I can't be of more help.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Sigh, it's strange. She used to pester my office daily. Now the silence is... louder than I expected.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I suppose the great General Augustus is ascending. Soon, she won't have time for old distractions.

steps.speaker: Owner
steps.content: Heh...

steps.speaker: Owner
steps.content: It's only... she was saying something similar not long ago. That "once the war ended, the Chief of Minos became a ghost. A fair-weather friend, tossing allies aside once the fighting's done."

options: My loyalty was never in question.

choices.text: My loyalty was never in question.

steps.content: Smiling, she offers you another glass.

steps.speaker: Owner
steps.content: It may not be my place to say, but I believe she keeps her distance precisely because she values the connection so much.

steps.speaker: Owner
steps.content: She's afraid of losing you.
The small terminal happens to be tuned to today's breaking news.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Hyenas... maggots... beasts of the Sillage Society. You've trampled lives, stolen the city's noble cause, and manipulated the loyalty of better men and women. You've embedded yourselves like parasites, sucking this city dry for far too long.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: But now... the troop of ghosts has returned from hell. The time for reckoning is here. And I will see to it... until the end!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...So entangled with all that power. It's a side of her I never had to see.

steps.speaker: Owner
steps.content: But she's also the same hero she's always been.
She stares into the terminal, the candle's flame flickering a silent dance in her eyes.

steps.speaker: Owner
steps.content: ...They're hailed as heroes, but only when the city needs them. They're polished up and put on the front line, a shield against the bullets in the name of glory.

steps.speaker: Owner
steps.content: And when the war is over? The same voices that praised them now cry for "reflection," and spit on the very monuments they built.

steps.speaker: Owner
steps.content: This time, at least, she is powerful. Too powerful to be cast aside. She can now remind them where a hero truly belongs.

steps.speaker: Owner
steps.content: Well... I imagine the general would say...

steps.speaker: Owner & ${PlayerName}
steps.content: "Who? Why should I care?"
You speak in perfect unison, and your smiles lock. As you take another sip of your drink, a pleasant tipsiness starts to wash over you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...I think I understand why she likes this place. Out there, it's all turmoil and chaos. But in here... it's a safe harbor.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: If possible, I'd like to become a regular here, too.

steps.speaker: Owner
steps.content: The honor would be mine. And with you here, I'm certain the general would find her way back more often.
A laugh escapes you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Yeah... I have plenty of ideas for how to make her visits "voluntary."
BAM! The door slams open. Augustus stands there, her face livid as she glares at you both.
A furious roar answers you, followed by the deadly hiss of steel leaving its scabbard.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Stay away from him!!

steps.speaker: Owner
steps.content: Argh—!

She flings her sword, guiding it toward you with her magnetic power. On the counter, a dozen bottles of aged liquor shatter, their contents coalescing into several Underground Puppets that lunge your way.
Augustus scans the room for more weapons, but finds only the small music terminal—nothing of the iron or steel that she can command.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: ${PlayerName}!!!
Your shackles barely deflect the first attack. It's not nearly enough. Augustus still stands at a distance from you, but for her, that's well within range.

You yank the bag from your side and shake it violently, scattering all the "secret weapons" across the floor—bullets, knives, forks, all made of metal. Augustus freezes for a split second, then understands. Her power engages.
The Puppets surge. Two forks hook into your collar, yanking you backward from the assault. You stumble, falling directly into Augustus's waiting arms.
You look up. A few other knives hover in the air between you and the Puppets, holding them at bay.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Hold them back! Buy some time!
[Release the shackles]
Your shackles buy you three seconds. Just enough. You feel Augustus's grip tighten, her body tense. Then, a powerful energy explosion erupts.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Take them down!
CRASH! A luxury car plows through the wall, instantly crushing three Puppets. Right behind it, a squad of Shattered Blade soldiers storms the ruined bar.

steps.speaker: Soldiers
steps.content: Roger that!
[Action sequence]

The chaos is swiftly subdued. The Puppets are neutralized, their threat extinguished in a flurry of efficient violence. The owner is hauled from the wreckage of her collapsed and contaminated liquor cabinet, her gaze finding you with a desperate plea.

steps.speaker: Owner
steps.content: Catherine... I...

steps.speaker: Iron Mask
steps.content: Take her away.

Around you, the soldiers conduct a methodical inventory of the aftermath: the faint taint of the Underground sorcery, the lingering residue of the Sillage, and the trails of covert communications. Throughout it all, Augustus remains a constant, tense presence at your side, never straying more than a step away.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: ...When did you know?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: When Clerk Barry was attacked. Your reaction wasn't just about my safety. You were furious that innocent people were getting hurt... and shaken by someone's betrayal.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: That's when I realized your anonymous bulk-buying of his book wasn't a joke. It was a shield. You didn't want to publicly endorse him, and this bar was the only loose thread.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'm the one who pulled it. I stumbled onto the truth and had no idea how dangerous that was.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And being here just confirms it...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Everything in this place is non-magnetic. She'd rather polish silver than have a single piece of steel. Candles over electric lights. She was never on your side.
You feed her the facts like a steady drip, your voice a firm anchor as Augustus pulls the fragments of her composure back together.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: After Barry was attacked, you figured it out too, didn't you? That's why you never came back... Were you planning to handle her yourself? Did I get in your way?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: ...If you knew she was suspicious, why come here alone?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I bet that you would come for me.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: You gambled with your life? Have you lost your mind?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Yes. I specifically gambled that you would protect it.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content:
Even with your power grab underway, you don't want me dead. You don't want me ending up like Victor.
That's good. Because I don't want to end up like Adrian either, slowly pushed out of your life.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Neither of us wants to see you on that battlefield alone. Not like Dravyn.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: ...That old man. What did Adrian tell you?
You bite back the words—that the Commander-in-Chief called her an arrogant, annoying brat. Some truths are better left unsaid.

The Commander-in-Chief brought letters spanning two decades. They told a story: of two men mourning fallen comrades, raging against betrayals. Then, the gradual emergence of differences leading to the Marshal's complete isolation. Adrian's final, confidential letter never even made it to his desk.

Barry's documentary is incisive, but it's no substitute for the living accounts, for walking the same paths. Only then can you glimpse the true past and peer through the rift into this city's deeper truth.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I used to think the strong craved power. But watching you... I've realized it's not that simple. Power also craves the strong.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Even those in the shadows need a figurehead to clear their path. Those who failed to kill you now covet your influence. They'll try to seduce you, break you, or own you. It's a trap designed specifically for prey like you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You see it, don't you? The same web that caught Dravyn is laid right at your feet. Do you really plan to walk into it?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: ...Don't underestimate me. There's no web I can't tear apart, no dead end I can't breach.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: I'm just disgusted by the enemy's shamelessness. This is the most revolting battle I've ever fought.
Augustus's gaze sweeps over the wreckage: the splintered bar, the glittering carpet of glass, the void where the owner once held court. A silent storm of emotions passes over her face.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: This was a good place. Whenever the outside world sickened me—when I had to stop myself from slaughtering those maggots, when I was in a foul mood and couldn't find you... I'd come here. Have a drink. Chat with her. It helped me breathe.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: They wouldn't even leave me this one small sanctuary.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: ...I can't kill her. She's Brock's niece, his only living relative.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: I held her when she was born. The Independence Army raised her together. Before my cryosleep, she gave me flowers. Her parents were imprisoned for opposing Dravyn... I have to look after her. But more than that...

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Whenever I grew tired of this new era, I'd come here to remember. It's the last place left from the old days. And those worms found even this... corrupted even her...

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: You see, ${PlayerName}, how clever my enemy is. They flatter me to lower my guard, then target everyone around me to isolate me. They won't even grant me a moment's peace.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: This is DisCity, the world's glittering peak. A throne of money and power everyone scrambles for. And it doesn't matter who sits on it. Victor, Adrian... Dravyn... it's all the same.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: ...Quite the battlefield, isn't it? More treacherous than the war you just fought. I intend to win, but I can't keep my hands as clean as you'd like.
The candlelight flickers, and though her face remains shrouded in shadow, you feel you have finally traced the contours of the person within.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The victory the Independence Army bought with their lives was stolen and twisted. Now history's repeating. You can't stand it. You want to crush these enemies, but you're terrified of walking Dravyn's same path... Am I right?
Her silence is confirmation enough.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You've always been a warrior who defies fate. I'm in no position to judge your chosen battlefield... Let's just say I want to understand more.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: As you said, this is the center of the world. It gathers all the wealth, dreams, glory, and filth. It has its own rules. The higher you climb, the darker and more dangerous it gets. It's a suffocating mess.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: If a great general plans to break this cycle by carrying the entire city-state on her shoulders... I have to wonder...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Back then, you commanded an army and bore all their suffering and sins. Now you want to command the greatest city-state, which means carrying all its prosperity and corruption... Can one person really bear that weight?
Your eyes have adjusted to the dark, and now you can truly see her. The bloodstained ferocity has drained from her gaze, leaving only a deep, serene blue that lingers in the shadows.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: ...I can answer that, wise Shepherd. I've asked myself the same thing countless times.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: I've never feared taking power or stepping onto this shadowy battlefield. I swear I'll be victorious. I won't fall to any enemy, and I won't compromise who I am.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: But I'm not foolish enough to fight alone. I'll have extraordinary warriors as my mind, my blade, and my shield. And you... you will be my shackles and my scabbard.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: All of you make me stronger. Far superior to those cowards. Victory will be mine. That's the resolve I bring to this fight.
As she speaks, the serene blue of her eyes slowly churns with a gathering storm.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: ...But it's all so tedious. So shameless. How can it be this ugly? There are no warriors willing to die for this city, no souls with the resolve to face death without flinching.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Nothing but self-serving vultures. No principles, no convictions. Having to maneuver among them... it turns my stomach.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: This battle isn't worth my passion, and today's DisCity isn't worth my soldiers' lives. Only a stubborn fool like Dravyn would cling to it so desperately, not letting go even at the end.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Rather than worrying that power will corrupt me, you should worry I'll lose all patience with this farce and flip the entire board.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...It sounds like you're the one worried you might do that.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: For someone about to charge into battle, you're being unusually cautious. That's not like you, General.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But now I know what I can do for you.
You sit up straight and grasp the empty scabbard she left in your hands.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: No one in this world can stop you from fighting. But I hope one day you can leave this battlefield you hate. Let your subordinates or allies win your victories for you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I can't do that for you. I have my own battles to fight.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But I will protect you. If DisCity's blade ever starts to break—if you ever verge on rampage—I will find you. I will stop you. I'll do whatever it takes to make you stand down... even if it means following the path you took when you killed Dravyn with your own hands.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Your sword once cleared a path for me. So from now on, no matter what battlefield you march onto... as long as I hold this scabbard, I won't let you become something you'd despise.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: ...Heh, well said.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: What a speech...
She composes herself, rises, and helps you to your feet. After straightening your clothes, she leads you from the battle-ravaged quiet of the bar into the silence of another car.

The engine stirs, and you plunge into the night. No Shattered Blade soldiers follow; this journey is for you two alone. The vast cityscape streams past on both sides, a familiar tableau—just like your first meeting, just like every encounter yet to come.

But tonight, your vision has changed. The dense high-rises no longer just cradle countless lights; they trace the edges of a massive silhouette. It looms like a primordial beast, bearing festering wounds a century old, its body slowly swelling with a breath like the eternal rhythm of tides.

And against this colossal shadow draped across your path, everything else diminishes—the car carrying you, the General's sword, your seemingly resolute promise—all of it shrinks into fleeting smallness, like a sigh dissolving into the wind.
[Scene Change] MBCC
The journey ends where it so often does: she returns you to the familiar grounds of the Bureau, a place that has come to feel like home.
With a final word of farewell, Augustus watches you step out.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: I have my soldiers, and I will eventually claim my battlefield. But you...

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: A scabbard doesn't need to kill. With you here, the Rancors will never bend, never corrode, never run wild. So... you have to stay alive.

A small smile touches her lips. She takes off her hat and places it on your head, pressing the brim down to steal your vision. You expect this to be like all the times before—her signature prelude to a tease, a final, flippant gesture to lighten a heavy moment.

But this time is different. Blinded by the fabric and shadow, you feel her hand firm on your shoulder, pulling you close. She leans in, and her voice, a low vibration in your ear, is unnervingly deep.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: ...Stay alive. Whatever comes, you won't have to face it. I promise you that.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Then I promise you, too.

options: Even on different battlefields, I'll be watching.
You have my word. As your scabbard.

steps.content: Is that a smile? You can't be sure. But you feel the brief, telling pressure of her grip on your shoulder before she releases you. Only then does the car pull away, leaving you in its wake.
[Scene Change: Eastside]

The steel storm does not immediately subside. It rages on, a tempest unleashed after years of pent-up fury, scouring the city streets. In its wake, many vanish; many more flee. Only after days of unrelenting terror does the Shattered Blade abruptly withdraw.
Then, some of the vanished are returned to their homes, dazed and silent. Others are found bound at the prison gates. Many bear notes affixed to them.

<color=#fb9259><i><size=40>
"To our gracious hosts, thank you for the warm welcome. I simply had to return the favor with a surprise party of my own.
You all played your parts well. My thanks for the participation.

I'll leave the cleanup to you, the esteemed 'city-state.' I'm sure your experts will know exactly how to handle the legal aftermath."

<color=#fb9259><i><size=40>
"After all... I might just come back on a whim."

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: The higher-ups have dispatched additional personnel to assist with our workload. It's a significant show of support. We have been given strict instructions to alleviate your administrative burden, Chief, and to ensure you maintain a healthier work-life balance.
Despite your deep bewilderment, you accept the unprecedented directive:

<i><size=40>
Your scheduled duty is limited to 8 hours per day, 5 days per week, with compensatory leave for any overtime.
You are allocated 40 days of annual leave, with permission to be absent when the workload is light.
Oh, and one more thing.
No external department can task you with assignments without proper approval.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Am I dreaming? What kind of prank is this? Who signed off on this... an angel?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: ...It's authentic, Chief. We have already begun rerouting several assistance requests from the 9th Agency. The directive comes directly from <color=#fb9259>EDGE</color>.

EDGE-03: Is this really your solution to quell the unrest? An EDGE seat carries significant weight. It must be granted through consensus and with extreme caution.
EDGE-07: The original candidate is already paralyzed with fear. Acting now is damage control. We can't allow her to create greater complications.
EDGE-03: But this is coercion. Her terrorist acts, mimicking Dravyn's methods, were likely orchestrated precisely for this purpose. Yield once, and this tactic will repeat indefinitely.
EDGE-03: We still possess the capability to stop her. For now, at least.

EDGE-02: If you're referring to the shackles, I suggest keeping those two separated. In the current situation, trying to restrain her might result in even SHP-13 being swayed to her side. The cost would far outweigh any benefit.
EDGE-02: The current arrangement isn't so bad, is it?

EDGE-05: Precisely. DisCity requires her protection, and we cannot risk her turning her blade toward the upper echelons at this juncture.
EDGE-05: If she has grown weary of the theater below and wishes to play at our level, so be it. The strategic advantage remains ours.
EDGE-05: Much like when we established the FAC, or reorganized EDGE... would you not agree?
EDGE-05: Besides, 01 still possesses the means to redirect her focus when necessary.

EDGE-05: Have you circulated new intelligence regarding the missing overseas troops again?

EDGE-01: In a manner of speaking.
EDGE-01: However, she also made it clear she has no interest in wasting time with our "pointless deliberations." For her first meeting, she asked me to deliver only two statements on her behalf.

EDGE-08 [Proxy]: The blade has returned, now hanging above your heads.
EDGE-08 [Proxy]: You'd better all watch your steps.
